newsitem.title: USA: Wash. legislature passes budget, governor to sign.
newsitem.headline: Wash. legislature passes budget, governor to sign.

text.p: Washington Gov. Gary Locke and Republican state legislators have agreed to a budget compromise, clearing the way for adjournment of the 1997 legislative session, state officials said on Sunday.
In quick succession on Saturday, the state House and Senate passed a $19.07 billion spending plan to cover the next two years.
Democratic Gov. Locke, who vetoed the legislature's first budget proposal last week, plans to sign this version, his office said Sunday.
State lawmakers dipped into the $500 million reserve fund they wrote into their first budget to add funding for various programs identified by the governor.

The final budget compromise includes millions of dollars more for health insurance subsidies for the working poor, social workers, life-saving drugs for people with AIDS, and worker retraining programs.
In the new spending plan, the budget reserve shrinks to $362 million. The level of business and property tax cuts stays the same at $393 million.

"We kept our promise to reduce taxes so that the economy of the state of Washington can continue to thrive so we have more money in the future to meet the needs of the people of Washington," said state Senator Jim West, the Republican budget committee chairman.
